British police said on Thursday they had arrested a man after a local government representative was stabbed on the streets of the city of Bradford in northern England. The 52-year-old councillor was found with serious injuries after the stabbing on a residential street on Thursday morning, West Yorkshire Police said. The man “was taken to hospital where his condition is described as serious but not life-threatening”, the police statement said. A 32-year-old man suspected of the attack fled to a roof but was later brought down and charged with attempted murder. Police said: “There is no information to suggest that this is a politically motivated incident at this time.” Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources The victim was named by the media as Councillor Ibrar Ali, a member of Your Bradford Independent group, which has 10 councillors, unpaid democratically elected representatives in local government. 87-year-old arraigned for attempting to murder Adamawa judge Police arraign 87-year-old man over attempted murder of Adamawa judge Kebbi man arrested for attempted murder, robbery of commercial motorcyclist Your Bradford Independent Group was supported in May elections by Your Party, a left-wing political party co-founded by veteran British socialist Jeremy Corbyn. Ali was due to hold a meeting with locals on Saturday, which has been cancelled, according to the district council’s website. Bradford has a population of around half a million and around 30 per cent of residents are Muslim. The leader of Bradford’s council is from the hard-right anti-immigrant Reform party. The head of the council’s Labour faction, Imran Khan, posted on Facebook that he was “horrified by this horrendous incident”. AFP Kindly share this story:
